title: What Are You Really Paying For Reddit's Ad Growth?
summary: Reddit (RDDT) stock is down about 35% over the past twelve months. Yet at about $155 it still trades at about 26.5 times trailing adjusted earnings, meaning normalized net income with stock-based compensation added back. The forecast that makes Reddit look cheaper does not need wider margins. It needs advertising to keep growing while search referrals stay volatile.

title: How Far Could Alphabet Stock Move On You In A Year?
summary: Alphabet (GOOGL) stock trades at about $332, and options expiring roughly a year out price a 68% probability range running from roughly $233 to roughly $474. That floor sits just under the stock's 52-week low of $235.96, while the ceiling clears its 52-week high of $402.12. Yet, a range this wide is close to normal for these shares, not a sign of unusual fear.
